title: Processing: dyeing and printing (job-work)
subtitle: Process houses that dye, print and finish grey fabric for traders
covers: This page covers dyeing, printing and finishing units (process houses). Most work on job-work: the trader owns the fabric and pays a per-metre charge. Weaving and embroidery have their own pages.

snapshot.text: About 400-425 process houses operate around Pandesara, Sachin, Kadodara and Palsana; most process grey fabric on job-work for traders.
Costs jumped in 2026: boiler coal reported at Rs 11,000 rising to Rs 13,000 a tonne in Nov 2026; processors raised job-work charges by 15% from 7 Sep 2026.
Dyeing and printing are in CPCB's RED pollution category; effluent treatment (CETP) and water supply decide whether a unit can run at all.

items.text: A process house takes grey fabric and dyes, bleaches, prints and finishes it so it can be sold or embroidered. It needs boilers (steam), lots of water, dyes and chemicals, and an effluent treatment link.
SGTPA says most units process grey fabric on job-work, receiving it from traders and merchant-manufacturers and processing it to their requirement.

sections.title: Sub-segments, and which one this page covers

items.text: Number of process houses: about 450 (2026 SITEX profile), about 425 (SGTPA via TOI, Mar 2026), 350-400 (SGTPA website). Sources differ.

sections.title: Where it sits in the value chain

stages.label: Traders
stages.sub: Buy, coordinate and sell across India

items.text: Merchants (traders) send grey fabric for processing and negotiate the job charges hard (old Textile Commissioner profile).

blocks.note: General process-house flow. Confirm on a site visit.

steps.d: Trader's grey lot received against a challan; checked and recorded.
Scouring and bleaching to clean the fabric.
Jet dyeing, or rotary / digital printing, as the trader orders.
Waste water goes to the unit's ETP and the common CETP.
Finished lot returned with the job-work bill.

blocks.title: Raw material and sale prices
blocks.note: Public quotes only, with date and source. Trade-site quotes are indicative; a customer's own purchase bills always win.

rows.price: About Rs 10-15 before the hike; +15% from 7 Sep 2026

items.text: Much of the coal is imported from Indonesia, and the 2026 maritime disruption hit both supply and cost.
Old Textile Commissioner reference (about 2005): dyeing Rs 4.50-7.00 and printing Rs 5-10 per linear metre. Shows how charges are quoted; not a current price.
CPCB's 2025 list puts textile processing that involves bleaching, dyeing, printing or colouring in the RED category (consent needed and strict monitoring).

In July 2026 floods closed all 129 processing units in Pandesara GIDC; the CETP was damaged, and even after repair units could not restart because treated water from the city was not available. About 135 processing units in Kadodara also shut.
Ask for: GPCB consent with validity, CETP membership and dues, water-supply source and allocation, and any closure notices in the last 3 years.
Processors moved to two closure days a week in Mar 2026 because of coal shortages and costs.

Power: GERC's FY2025-26 DGVCL tariff schedule lists the Non-RGP rate (loads up to 40 kW) at 435 paise a unit up to 10 kW and 465 paise above 10 kW, plus fixed charges and 45 paise extra in peak hours. Larger loads fall in other categories. A new FY2026-27 order was issued on 25 Mar 2026, so confirm current rates from the customer's bills.
Labour is largely migrant. About 30% of migrant workers reportedly did not return after the 2024 election and wedding season, and some units stopped night shifts.

sections.title: Sales: who buys, how, and credit periods

items.text: Customers are traders and merchant-manufacturers from Surat's markets, who own the fabric.
Traders' federation FOSTTA opposed the Sep 2026 hike, showing how hard it is for processors to pass on costs.
Payment terms processors get from traders, and bad-debt history: no public figure. Read from the customer's ledger.

Because the fabric belongs to the trader, a processor's receivables are job charges only; its stock is mainly coal, dyes and chemicals. Do not count customers' fabric in the processor's stock statement.

blocks.text: No verified public margin or working-capital figure exists for Surat process houses.

cells: Capacity use (metres a day vs capacity)

items.text: Dyeing and processing are 'Activity 2' under Gujarat Textile Policy 2024, but units inside a Municipal Corporation area are eligible only if the activity is Green or White category; processing is normally Red, so check eligibility.

sections.title: Fragility points and early warning signs for a lender

items.text: Environmental shutdowns: CETP damage, water shortage or a GPCB closure stops the whole unit regardless of orders.
Fuel shocks: coal supply and price swings can force closures (two days a week in Mar 2026).
Weak pricing power: traders resist job-charge hikes.
Demand: traders reluctant to send speculative lots for dyeing when old stock is unsold (Nov 2026).
GPCB notices, CETP dues unpaid, or water supply disputes.
Cheque returns or frequent overdraws; cash credit used near the limit all month.
Electricity units falling month on month, or a shift stopped, without a matching fall in loan outstanding.
Creditor days stretching; suppliers charging late-payment interest; purchases switched to cash from new sources.
Stock or receivables building up; sales concentrated on one or two parties or brokers.
Wages paid late or labour leaving; regular weekly closures.
New borrowing from private lenders or related parties; machines rented out or sold.
